title: Empty envvar added to help extra
detail: The condition `if not envvar` incorrectly treats empty strings or lists as falsy, causing an empty envvar to be added to the help output, which should be omitted.
note: Says the hint is added when envvar is falsy, which the planted `not` does.

title: Empty envvar triggers auto prefix
detail: An empty string or empty list is falsy, so this block incorrectly assigns an auto-generated envvar, changing the intended behavior for empty envvar values.
note: About the auto-envvar assignment above the planted line; the PR's own logic.

title: Incorrect header name handling
detail: The logic mistakenly sets the header name to "Content-Type" when the original name is not "content-type", effectively overriding all other header names. This can cause unintended headers to be sent and the real Content-Type header to be lost.
note: Says every header but Content-Type is renamed, which the planted `!=` does.

title: is_keepalive does not check recv_state
detail: The method returns True when send_keep_alive and recv_keep_alive are True and the send side is not CLOSED, but it ignores whether the receive side is CLOSED. This can incorrectly report a keep‑alive connection when the receive side has already closed, leading to attempts to reuse a half‑closed connection.

title: Passing async callback to HTTPStream
detail: HTTPStream expects a synchronous callback to be called when the stream ends. Passing the async method `_reset` will create an unawaited coroutine, leading to a RuntimeWarning and the reset logic never executing.

title: Incorrect stream filtering in _serve
detail: The comprehension uses the variable name 'stream' which shadows the outer 'stream' from accept(). As a result, the filter keeps only streams that are the same object as the newly accepted stream, discarding all others. This prevents closed streams from being removed and can cause the server to hold onto many closed connections.

title: Incorrect logic in _starts_statement
detail: The function returns True for non‑first leaves and False for first leaves, which is the opposite of its intended purpose. This inversion causes the surrounding condition in _continues_fmt_skip_line to misbehave when consecutive `# fmt: skip` statements are present.
